item.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed for 1st time in history
item.description: For the first time in history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, Macy's said Wednesday.

item.title: Iran denounces U.S. use of AI in war
item.description: Iran's U.N. envoy claims the U.S. military used Palantir and Anthropic AI systems to select some 2,000 targets over just four days.

item.title: Would A Brain Surgeon Let His Kids Play Football?
item.description: A new study of 235 donated NFL brains found CTE in 215 of them. Dr. Myron Rolle is a former college All-American and NFL player who is now a pediatric neurosurgeon. We ask him about his experience, his expertise and the advice he gives to parents when they ask if America's most popular pastime can still be made safe enough for our children. If you'd like to share your own great question, email us at greatquestion@cbsnews.com.

item.title: Steelers releasing quarterback Aaron Rodgers, reports say
item.description: The Steelers are releasing quarterback Aaron Rodgers after he was benched for Friday's game, multiple reports say. Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday and said he wouldn't return to the Steelers while taking shots at head coach Mike McCarthy. CBS Sports HQ NFL analyst Emory Hunt has more.

item.title: Stocks turn volatile as Jensen Huang rebound rally fades
item.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq index fell more than 1,000 points in early trading before clawing back most of the losses.

item.title: Maps show where Thanksgiving storms could disrupt holiday
item.description: Rain, snow and powerful winds were forecast to impact large stretches of the country on Thanksgiving, potentially disrupting holiday festivities and, in some areas, hampering travel plans.

item.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed due to coastal storm
item.description: The 100th edition of Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City has been postponed until Saturday due to a coastal storm. Tom Hanson has the details.

item.title: China may have surveilled Alice Huang amid affair with Nvidia CEO
item.description: China's Ministry of State Security may have been surveilling Alice Huang and sought information from her after her affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang began, U.S. officials told congressional staffers.

item.title: Blindsided by Iowa detonation, White House scrambled, sources say
item.description: White House officials have expressed frustration in internal conversations that they had to scramble to deal with the crisis.

item.title: Most Polymarket users lost money betting on the U.S. midterms
item.description: More than half of Polymarket accounts lost money betting on the U.S. midterm elections, according to one analysis.

item.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan for 1 million data center satellites
item.description: In an X post on Wednesday, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the satellites will be a "great asset to America and the world."

item.title: Vance says Nvidia's Huang isn't under investigation, doesn't need a pardon
item.description: Vice President JD Vance said he was assured Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang isn't under federal investigation.

item.title: Leaked data shows 490,000 Russian forces have died in Ukraine war
item.description: Russian government data obtained by pro-Ukraine hackers and analyzed by the BBC indicates that Russia has lost at least 490,334 soldiers during its war on Ukraine.

item.title: More than 490,000 Russian soldiers have died in Ukraine war, leaked data suggests
item.description: More than 490,000 Russian soldiers have died since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, according to leaked Russian government data analyzed by CBS News partner network BBC News. CBS News' Aidan Stretch has more.

item.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaves U.S. and arrives in Spain
item.description: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the El Salvador native who was mistakenly deported last year, left the U.S. for Spain on Tuesday, the Department of Homeland Security confirmed.

item.title: Why are investors freaking out even as the U.S. economy surges?
item.description: The economy is sending mixed signals, with growth jumping while stocks gyrate. Here's what economists say is going on.

item.title: "Narco sub" seized in Atlantic but no drugs found on board
item.description: The operation was carried out in cooperation with the Colombian navy and the U.S. Joint Interagency Task Force South.

item.title: Maps show Iowa lead dust plume possibly drifting into Missouri after Army detonation
item.description: Maps released by the Army Tuesday show a possible plume of toxic dust after its detonation of munitions in Iowa drifting southwest toward northeast Missouri between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. Wednesday.

item.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia releases statement after leaving U.S. for Spain
item.description: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the El Salvador native who was mistakenly deported by ICE last year, left the U.S. for Spain. CBS News' Camilo Montoya Galvez has more.

item.title: Army detonates toxic explosives at Iowa plant despite concerns
item.description: The U.S. Army detonated a stockpile of degrading explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa on Wednesday, after days of back-and-forth between politicians and the courts.

item.title: Army calls controlled detonation of unstable lead explosives in Iowa "tremendously successful"
item.description: U.S. Army representatives spoke to reporters on Wednesday after a controlled detonation in Iowa of toxic lead munitions, calling the operation "tremendously successful" despite questions surrounding public health. CBS News' Ian Lee reports.

item.title: Small plane crash off Mississippi kills 6, including 2 children
item.description: Six people, including two children, have been found dead after a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi, according to the Coast Guard.

item.title: Father of teen killed at campsite says it was "a deliberate act"
item.description: Carey Washington "Wash" Vinson, 19, was shot and killed while on an annual camping trip with friends in the Florida Panhandle.

item.title: High-quality medieval armor discovered in shipwreck that sank in 1495
item.description: The ship, known as "Griffin" or "Gribshunden," was the warship of Denmark's 15th-century leader King Hans.

item.title: Inside Trump's effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang's comeback as Nvidia CEO came after a weekend of strategizing by Trump administration officials, who offered assurances to the company.

item.title: Trump owned millions in Nvidia stock as he pressed for Jensen Huang's reinstatement
item.description: President Trump holds tens of millions in Nvidia shares, giving him a personal stake in the company's stock market roller coaster ride of the past two weeks, financial disclosure documents show.

item.title: Army to detonate unstable explosives in Iowa Wednesday morning
item.description: A federal appeals court on Monday declined to block the Army from detonating explosives containing lead azide at a munitions plant in Iowa.

item.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang still has security clearance, sources say
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche did not say whether federal investigators interviewed Jensen Huang — who was rehired as CEO on Monday — or examined his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.

item.title: Beauty products are getting more expensive. Here's what's driving the price increases
item.description: With rising transportation costs, tariffs, and higher raw material prices cutting into the bottom lines of companies across the industry, they can expect to pay more in the coming months.

item.title: Why Are We All So Thirsty For Reality TV Again? | Straight Up with Vlad and Kelly
item.description: "Dancing With the Stars" is breaking voting records even after 35 seasons, cringe "Love Is Blind" clips are breaking the internet, and "Love Island" is still breaking hearts week after week. It seems we are having a reality TV renaissance. But what's behind it? Are we yearning for people to be "real" and "messy" in an online world so otherwise polished? Or are we falling for a trap? Is reality TV the furthest thing from reality of all? Vlad and Kelly are breaking it down in the very first episode of Straight Up. We love a good cocktail on this show, but please drink responsibly: this content is for listeners 21 and over, so know your limits, enjoy in moderation, and always plan a safe ride home.
